requirement: The getting-started documentation MUST explain that the session-start hook tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation. The getting-started documentation MUST explain that the session-start hook tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill.

Two tests in `tests/repository.rs` cover it. Both carry `{test}` references to the subject and read the real files through `repository_file`. That helper uses `fs::read_to_string` on a path under `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`. Both tests loop over `README.md` and `md/getting_started.md`.

- **`getting_started_documents_symposium_setup_and_skill_migration`:**
  - It asserts that the text contains "session", "hook" and "`habeas` skill".
  - It also asserts that a single paragraph contains "hook tells", "load the `habeas` skill before starting any work" and "session". This ties the skill-loading instruction to the hook within one paragraph, so the words cannot be satisfied by unrelated mentions elsewhere in the file.
- **`installation_guides_cover_setup_hooks_refresh_and_preserving_local_skills`:**
  - It asserts that the text contains "load the `habeas` skill" and "advises the agent".
  - It asserts the exact README sentence: "Its session-start hook tells the agent that the project tracks requirements with Habeas and to load the `habeas` skill before starting any work."
  - It asserts the exact guide sentence: "When an agent starts a session in this project, Habeas's hook tells it … to load the `habeas` skill before starting any work."

I confirmed that `md/getting_started.md` contains that paragraph. A test failure on a missing or altered sentence would catch removal or alteration of the explanation.

The tests also check other behaviour: the conditional `habeas setup` advice, sync and refresh guidance, and local-skill migration. These belong to the parent requirement `requirements.install.symposium` and are not needed for this subject. I found no gap in how the tests check this requirement.
